description: In the northern sky, warriors choose the dead to populate Valhalla. Their army must face the twilight of the gods.

hero.hook: Dying with a sword in your hand is not an end: it is a selection for the last war of the world.

blocks.text: In Norse mythology, death in battle is not an end. This is a **selection**. The **Valkyries**, whose name means “those who choose killings,” roam the battlefields for Odin, the sovereign god.

Their mission: to take the bravest to the **Valhalla**, the “killing room”. This palace is not a paradise of rest. It is a celestial barracks. Because Odin is preparing an army for , the final battle that will destroy the world and kill the gods. [[Ragnarök]]

**Odin** knows the prophecy. At , giants and monsters will descend on , the home of the gods. To delay the inevitable, he needs elite soldiers: the **Einherjar**, “those who fight alone”. [[Ragnarök]] [[Asgard]]

blocks.caption: Odin, master of the gods, haunted by the end of the world.

blocks.text: Valhalla only held **half** of the warriors who died in battle. The other half joined the Fólkvangr, domain of the goddess **Freyja**. Even after a heroic death, heroes were divided.

Valhalla, in Asgard, has **540 gates**. Each is large enough for eight hundred fighters to pass abreast. Only those who fell courageously, sword in hand, are entitled to it. The Valkyries sort things out from the sky.

The modern image of Valkyries often comes from 19th century romanticism: gentle virgins on horseback. Ancient texts, like the [[Poetic Edda]], paint much harsher figures. They are linked to crows, birds of corpses. Some poems show them as macabre spinners: their threads are guts, their weights are heads.

blocks.caption: Valkyrie in flight: messenger of Odin and provider of heroes.

blocks.text: Figures like **Brynhildr** or  also have a human face: they hesitate between Odin's orders and their feelings for mortals. In Valhalla, their role changes. They leave the armor to serve mead to the heroes. The gesture speaks of recognition: the brave dead has become the elite of Asgard. [[Sigrun]]

In Valhalla, there is no peaceful retreat. At the crowing of the cock , the Einherjar arm themselves and kill each other on the plain of . In the evening, the wounds close. The dead rise again. Then comes the feast. [[Gullinkambi]] [[Idavoll]]

blocks.caption: The feast of the Einherjar: combat by day, banquets by night.

blocks.text: The wild boar **Sæhrímnir** is boiled every day by the cook, then reborn. Mead flows from the udders of the [[Andhrímnir]] goat. The Viking Paradise is a permanent training room. [[Heidrun]]
This cycle of violence and pleasure unites Odin's army. Centuries of friendly battles before the real enemy.

sections.title: Every day to fight, every evening to celebrate

blocks.text: This vision of the afterlife marked Viking Scandinavia. Physical courage was valued. Dying of old age or illness, the "straw death", led to **Hel**, a dull kingdom. It was better to fall with weapons in hand.

The Valkyrie has spanned the centuries. Richard Wagner fixed it in European memory with the . Today, she has become an archetype of a powerful woman, often far from her primary function: provider of corpses for a god who is plotting his own end. [[The Ride of the Valkyries (Wagner)]]

The **Valkyries** are recruiting the best dead for the **Valhalla**. There, the Einherjar fight and feast endlessly, in preparation for the . The Nordic paradise is a barracks, not a refuge. [[Ragnarök]]

sections.title: A dignified death rather than a “straw death”
